name: JExec Admissibility Standard (JAS)
definition: Four levels grading how governed a system's executions are before they mutate state. A level is a property of an execution path, not of an organization.
certification: None. JAS is a self-assessment specification. No certificate exists and none may be claimed.

levels.name: Ungoverned
levels.summary: No admissibility decision exists before execution; governance is post-hoc (logs, alerts, incident review).

levels.name: Declared
levels.test: Every execution states the seven fields before it runs.
levels.summary: Intent, actor, authority, scope, evidence, risk, and intended decision are declared and stored before execution. Nothing is yet verified.
requirements: All seven JExec Record fields declared before every execution on the path

levels.name: Verified
levels.test: Declarations are authenticated, checked, and recorded.
levels.summary: Actor identity authenticated; authority verified with scope comparison; evidence bound to content and current; a JExec Record stored for every decision including allows.
requirements: Authenticated per-actor identity, including per-agent identity
Verified authority with named source, verifier, and scope-coverage comparison
Evidence bound to content hashes or versions, with defined validity
A stored record for every decision, including allows

levels.name: Enforced
levels.test: A deny is structurally incapable of mutating state.
levels.summary: The verdict gates execution: deny blocks, escalate suspends until a distinct authority decides; irreversible classes gated asymmetrically; bypass lanes emit escalation records.
requirements: Verdicts computed by the published protocol rules
Deny structurally blocks the mutation; escalate suspends it
Asymmetric gating and declared reversal/review paths for irreversible risk classes
